meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France — national unitary jurisdiction (no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–France Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 30 May 1984; in force 21 May 1985)
France–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 26 November 2013; in force 1 December 2014)
France–United States Double Taxation Convention (signed 31 August 1994; amended by Protocols in 2006 and 2009)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49–54 — freedom of establishment for EU resident shareholders

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 (AML/CFT obligations), L.562-1 to L.562-14 (asset-freezing), and R.561-1 et seq.; UBO declaration regime under CMF Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and R.561-55 et seq.; beneficial-owner definitive thresholds under CMF Article R.561-1 (direct/indirect holding exceeding 25% of capital or voting rights); enforcement by ACPR, TRACFIN (Article L.561-23) and the Direction générale du Trésor; register administered by INPI as of 1 August 2023 pursuant to Décret n° 2021-738 of 8 June 2021 and the loi PACTE (Law n° 2019-486); restricted public access per Conseil d'État decision n° 474062 of 5 May 2023 consequent to the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted legitimate-interest access for regulated entities and persons demonstrating a legal interest per Conseil d'État ruling of 5 May 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copy of the proposed Gérant's passport (identity pages)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese notary office (公证处) in the holder's place of registration + PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs (办理附加证明书)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention, in force for China since 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence + PRC MFA or other designated apostille authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / criminal record certificate of the proposed Gérant (for non-French residents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau (公安机关) or judicial authority of the country of residence + competent apostille authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where apostille unavailable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Administration for Market Regulation (市场监督管理局) and/or company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction + competent apostille authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (executed by all shareholders) enabling a local formation agent to sign the draft statuts and effect registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese notary office (公证处) + PRC MFA apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers and UBOs against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists as given effect by directly applicable EU Regulations (notably Regulation (EC) No 881/2002, Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001); (iii) the national asset-freeze measures issued by the Direction générale du Trésor under CMF Articles L.562-1 to L.562-14 (published in the Official Journal, JORF); (iv) the OFAC SDN/Sanctions lists applied by French and correspondent banks to USD/PayPal clearing; and (v) politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in CMF Article L.561-10-1 and the FATF recommendations, using cross-lingual fuzzy matching on Latin/Chinese/Cyrillic script variants. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and, where required, TRACFIN declaration (CMF Article L.561-15).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises of INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for filing; preliminary name/trademark search on INPI data databases (https://data.inpi.fr) and the Registre National des Entreprises (https://www.inpi.fr); historical RCS/Kbis records held by the greffes des tribunaux de commerce (https://www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to CMF Article L.561-46 and Article L.123-1-2 of the Code de commerce, the corporate name must be composed of Latin-script characters (accented letters permitted in French); any foreign-language word in the name must be in Latin script (non-Latin characters such as Chinese ideograms are not admissible in the registered corporate denominação, but may be used as a commercial alias/sub-brand); the name must be preceded or followed by the legal form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the acronym 'SARL' and the amount of share capital (Article L.223-1 Code de commerce); documents filed at the registry must be in French (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994 — loi Toubon); a transliteration into French/English phonetics is therefore mandatory for any foreign-language brand element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying sovereign or public functions: 'République', 'Ministère', 'Préfecture', 'Mairie', 'Département', 'Région', 'National' (when implying State entity), 'Banque de France', 'Police', 'Gendarmerie'
Regulated financial/banking terms requiring prior ACPR authorization: 'Banque', 'Crédit', 'Finance', 'Assurance', 'Mutuelle', 'Courtier'
Regulated liberal professions requiring prior order approval: 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Expert-comptable', 'Commissaire aux comptes', 'Médecin', 'Architecte', 'Huissier'
Gaming-specific regulated token: 'Casino' — reserved for licensed gambling operators and requiring authorization from the Autorité Nationale des Jeux (ANJ) under the Code de la sécurité intérieure
Educational and health tokens: 'Académie', 'Université', 'Hôpital', 'Clinique' (requiring recteur or ARS approval)

Known third-party trade marks and famous names of game publishers/platforms (e.g., 'Nintendo', 'PlayStation', 'Epic Games', 'Ubisoft') — rejected on likelihood-of-confusion grounds and exposed to infringement actions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal pre-registration 'name reservation certificate': the name is frozen by publishing the draft statuts in a journal d'annonces légales (JAL) and retained for the subsequent registration filing. (1) Upon rejection (refus d'immatriculation) by the greffier, the applicant receives a written reasoned refusal and may, within 15 days, submit observations or file an amended application through the same guichet unique (regularization procedure per Code de commerce Article R.123-96). (2) If the refusal is based on identity/confusion with an existing company or trademark, the applicant may obtain a non-opposition/consent letter from the prior holder and re-file. (3) If the refusal persists, the applicant may bring an appeal (recours) before the President of the tribunal de commerce (or tribunal judiciaire) within whose jurisdiction the registered office is located, under the urgent ('référé') procedure, per Article R.123-96 of the Code de commerce; the court must decide as an urgency matter and the decision is appealable to the cour d'appel within 15 days. (4) Practically, the fastest remedy is selecting a new name and publishing a supplementary/amended JAL announcement (24–48 hours; approx. EUR 250–300), followed by immediate electronic re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation agréée per Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-3 to L.123-11-9 and R.123-170 et seq.) or, alternatively, the manager's French residential address for a maximum of 5 years (Article L.123-11-2). A bare virtual mailbox without a domiciliation contract is not admissible for RCS registration. For a B2B 3D-art outsourcing studio holding no retail licence, a domiciliation address (including at the gérant's residence) is acceptable to the greffe; the domiciliation contract or landlord's consent (acte de jouissance) must be filed with the registration package. The registered office must be able to receive official correspondence and service of process; there is no minimum staffing or physical square-footage requirement at pre-incorporation stage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 3–5% probability per annum of an unannounced on-site verification for a registered office domiciled at a commercial domiciliation provider, and less than 2% for a gérant's residential address; the greffier and INPI exercise document-based controls (postal audits, 'contrôles sur pièces') in the first year, while URSSAF payroll and DGCCRF B2B service inspections are estimated at 8–12% cumulative over the first 36 months for new service companies; the risk of a physical visit increases to 15–20% only if tax credits, employment declarations, or licence regimes are claimed. Full commercial substance (bank account, invoicing, subcontractor chain, insurance) is evidenced primarily through documentation rather than premises inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10, L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and R.223-1 to R.223-15; registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés under Articles R.123-30 et seq.; Guichet Unique implementing rules under Decree No. 2021-300.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the department of the registered office, acting through the national Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - single electronic dossier combining the M0 declaration with the signed Statuts (Articles of Association), culminating in the issuance of the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital (freely set in the articles; 1 EUR suffices) following the Loi PACTE 2019. Cash contributions must be released to at least 20% at incorporation, the balance within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully released immediately. The released amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a French bank or with a notary and can only be withdrawn after the Kbis is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST CONSTITUTIVE RESOLUTIONS OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF [NAME] SARL, dated [date]. The undersigned shareholders, acting as the sole constituent corporate organ, unanimously resolve: 1. The draft Articles of Association are adopted and forthwith constitute the Company. 2. The share capital of EUR X, divided into Y shares of EUR Z each, is hereby entirely subscribed; cash contributions have been duly paid into the Company's escrow bank account and the balance is callable within five years per Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code. 3. The registered office is definitively fixed at [address], France. 4. Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed as Gérant (statutory manager), accepting office, with full power to act on behalf of the Company except where the Articles reserve authority to shareholders. Adopted in [city] on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association and appointment of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The shareholders (private deed, sous seing privé) or, only where real estate is contributed, a French civil-law notary (notaire) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts (in French, or bilingual FR/EN for foreign partners) including the mandatory clauses of Article L.223-1 (corporate purpose, capital, shares, manager, profit appropriation, dissolution). Each shareholder signs every page with the mention 'lu et approuvé'. Appoint the Gérant in a separate deed or in the statuts; the Gérant must sign acceptance and a declaration of no criminal conviction. If in-kind or real-estate contributions are made, a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) must value them and a notarial deed is required.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (one original per shareholder plus a certified copy for the registry)
Deed of appointment of the Gérant with signed acceptance in French
Declaration under Article L.223-18 confirming the manager's legal capacity (foreign managers must prove no equivalent disqualification)
Copies of valid passports or national identity cards of all partners and the manager
Proof of residential address for each partner (under three months, with certified French translation if needed)
Certificate of no criminal record (bulletin n°3) or sworn declaration for the manager
Power of attorney (procuration) if the file is signed remotely
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a defective statutory clause, rectify it through a unanimous amendment (resolution constatant une erreur matérielle) signed by all shareholders and re-submit; notarial re-execution is required only when the original deed was notarial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the paid-in share capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French credit institution accepting the deposit, or the notary who drafted the deed, acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account ('compte de dépôt de fonds') in the name of the company in formation. Each shareholder transfers his cash contribution; the bank verifies that the released amount represents at least 20% of total cash capital and that in-kind contributions are fully furnished. The depositary issues the 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' (certificat du dépositaire) stating the amount deposited and the debit entries. These funds remain escrowed until the greffe registers the company, after which the manager withdraws them with proof of immatriculation.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts summarising the capital structure
Identity documents of all subscribing partners (passport or national ID)
Original deposit order (ordre de mouvement) and proof of wire transfer
Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the file or the attestation is rejected by the registry for missing mentions (amount, date, signatory designation), have the bank re-issue a corrected certificate; alternatively, re-deposit through a notaire acting as depositary under Article R.223-3.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory legal announcement in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French accredited legal announcements journal (JAL) authorised in the department of the registered office (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes, Le Journal Spécial des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert a formal announcement of incorporation containing the exact corporate name, form (SARL), capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, the manager's identity, and the competent registry court. The JAL publishes the notice and issues an 'attestation de parution' with the publication date and announcement number. Keep this attestation for the Guichet Unique submission.
required_dossiers: Completed announcement form supplied by the JAL
Project of statuts or a capital and management summary for the notice
Payment of publication fees (approximately 140-200 EUR excluding VAT, size-dependent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requests corrections (missing mandatory mentions under Article R.123-105), amend the notice and re-publish; the corrected attestation is then re-issued. A defective announcement cannot be cancelled retroactively, but the registry accepts a rectificative announcement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the full incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique / Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, transmitting electronically to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an electronic file on the Guichet Unique portal and complete the M0 declaration, entering all company data (name, form, capital, registered office, purpose, manager, duration, establishment address, legal status options). Upload the scanned constituent documents, pay the statutory fees online, and submit. The greffe reviews the file for legal compliance; on approval it records the company in the RCS and delivers the Extrait Kbis within about five business days.
required_dossiers: M0 company information form (electronic)
Signed statuts paginated and scanned
Acte de nomination du gérant and acceptance
Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds (escrow certificate)
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Proof of enjoyment of the registered office premises (signed lease, free occupation letter, or attestation de domiciliation)
Copy of the manager's passport and residential proof
Declaration of no criminal conviction (bulletin n°3)
Foreign partners' supporting documents with certified French translation
Power of attorney if the file is submitted through an intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is placed 'en observation' (suspension), the greffe notifies the defects; the applicant has 15 days to respond through the portal by uploading corrective documents. If immatriculation is refused, a new complete file may be submitted, or an appeal may be filed before the First President of the Court of Appeal within 15 days of notification (Article L.123-5-16).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of the Kbis and automatic tax and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Kbis) with automatic notifications to URSSAF, DGFiP, and the occupational health services for employers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registration is completed, retrieve the Extrait Kbis from the Guichet Unique portal or the greffe counter; verify the SIREN, SIRET, legal form and NAF/APE code. The company automatically receives its TVA intracommunautaire number (when applicable) from DGFiP, its URSSAF identifier, and, upon the first hiring, the employer account (LBM) with AER insurance. The escrowed capital can now be released; the manager withdraws it with the Kbis, finalises the corporate bank account, and orders corporate seals and letterheads.
required_dossiers: No further filing - rely on the Kbis and the automatic notifications issued by the portal
Keep the registration receipt for the escrow release
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors (typo in manager name or wrong APE), request a rectification from the greffe by written letter within three months, attaching supporting documents. If URSSAF or DGFiP identifiers are not received within 10 days, write to the relevant department enclosing the Kbis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DDETS) - labour inspection division; local fire prevention services (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours / Préfecture) for premises occupied by workers
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence exists for ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541430 (3D art outsourcing is a non-regulated commercial activity); the Extrait Kbis is the sole business permit. For the physical studio, a 'Déclaration d'ouverture d'établissement employant des salariés' and a conformity assessment under the French Labour Code (Articles R.4222-1 et seq. and R.4227-1 et seq.) must be in place before any employee occupies the premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (MTE) - Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) of the region where the studio is located
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EXEMPT - non-ICPE. The 3D art studio is not listed in the ICPE nomenclature (Code de l'environnement, Article R.511-9); no environmental authorisation, registration or impact assessment is required. Only the general duties of waste management (Article L.541-2) and connection to the municipal sanitation network apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluents or atmospheric emissions: sanitary waste-water must comply with municipal sewerage bylaws (décret n°94-469 water policy). Waste electrical and electronic equipment (DEEE - workstations, GPUs, monitors) must be transferred to an approved eco-organisation (éco-systèmes / Ecologic) with a tipping slip (bordereau de suivi de DEEE) kept on file; no VOC sources on site (no painting, no resin printing) and no hazardous waste threshold triggering a BSDI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety per Labour Code R.4227: annual inspection of fire extinguishers by an accredited body, emergency lighting, evacuation plan, two unobstructed exits, smoke detection where required; structural load certificate from a technical controller (bureau de contrôle) if installing heavy server or rendering racks or a mezzanine; the Single Occupational Risk Assessment Document (DUERP) finalised and registered with the occupational health service (SPST); workplace accessibility for disabled workers; and civil liability insurance covering the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French tax administration; online portal: impots.gouv.fr. Customs and export controls are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via the national single window DELTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor incorporating a French SARL registers through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; the registration file is transmitted to the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), which issues the statutory identifiers SIREN, SIRET, and APE/NAF code. The Greffe transmits the data to DGFiP, which automatically allocates the French intra-Community VAT identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) under Article 286 ter of the CGI. A non-resident foreign entity without a French permanent establishment that makes taxable supplies in France must file a direct application for VAT registration with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises using the official VAT registration form (Cerfa n°13789), and must appoint a fiscal representative established in France if it is outside the European Union. The application must identify the foreign entity, its foreign tax number, the nature of supplies, and the French agent or representative, after which the DGFiP issues a French VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A French SARL is by default a corporation subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its worldwide profits when its place of effective management is in France. It is not a pass-through entity by default. Territorial scope: French-resident IS taxpayers are taxed on worldwide income, with foreign branch income relieved by tax treaties or by the territoriality rules of Article 209 CGI where applicable. The SARL is not located in a tax-exempt zone and is not eligible for patent box treatment unless specific reduced rates for intellectual property apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not provide a check-the-box election. However, a SARL meeting the statutory conditions of Article 239 bis A CGI may elect to be taxed as a transparent partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) for a limited period, generally up to five fiscal years, if the members are individuals or eligible corporate shareholders. This option must be filed with DGFiP before the end of the relevant fiscal year. Additionally, a French parent company holding at least 95% of a subsidiary may elect l'intégration fiscale (fiscal integration), allowing a tax group to offset taxable profits and losses among members. Hybrid mismatch elections are not discretionary; France applies mandatory anti-hybrid rules under Article 212 bis CGI implementing ATAD, which override contractual classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general economic turnover threshold for a non-established foreign supplier making taxable supplies in France: VAT registration is required as soon as the first taxable supply is made unless an express exemption applies. For small French-established businesses, the franchise en base de TVA exemptions apply up to EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services per calendar year, but the franchise is an exemption, not a registration threshold. For intra-Community distance sales of goods by another EU taxable person, the statutory OSS distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000; sales below that threshold may remain subject to the supplier's home Member State VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting for domestic B2B transactions. The B2G segment already uses the Chorus Pro portal. In the B2B segment, all taxable persons established in France must, from 1 September 2026, issue electronic invoices through a certified dematerialization platform (PDP) or the public portal Chorus Pro, and simultaneously transmit invoice and transaction data to DGFiP under the e-invoicing/e-reporting reform. The reform will be phased for small enterprises from 1 September 2027. There is no per-transaction real-time fiscal stamping in the manner of a continuous clearance system; however, each invoice must contain the mandatory data set, including SIREN, SIRET, VAT identification number, invoice category, supply date, unit price, VAT amount, and a unique invoice number. Export invoices are reported on the French VAT return and, when relevant, in the French Intrastat/DEB declarations. Customs export declarations are processed electronically through the DELTA system with a valid MRN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union are zero-rated under Article 262 CGI when the supplier proves that the goods have physically left EU customs territory. The physical departure must generally occur within 90 days from the supply date, or within a longer contractual period not exceeding two years where the supply involves processing, assembly, or consignment. The 0% rate applies to the sale only if a valid customs export declaration has been accepted and the supplier holds transport documents evidencing exit from the EU. For services, B2B services supplied to a recipient established outside the EU are outside French VAT territorial scope under Article 259-1 CGI, and therefore not subject to French VAT, provided the supplier has obtained the recipient's valid foreign VAT or equivalent business registration number and contractual evidence. Offshore game 3D art outsourcing services to a non-EU game publisher can qualify as zero-rated or VAT-excluded services if the recipient is a business established outside the EU and the supply is not effectively linked to a French fixed establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Accepted customs export declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation / DEX) with a valid Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice (original) stating exporter, consignee, incoterms, value, nature of goods, and destination
Packing list detailing carton weights, counts, and shipping marks
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR/rail waybill evidencing physical transport from France or EU to a non-EU destination
Proof of arrival in the third country, such as customs entry declaration, port of destination confirmation, or delivery receipt
Intrastat / Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens (DEB) filing when the goods remain within EU statistical thresholds
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing receipt of export consideration within the statutory foreign-exchange repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and DGDDI cross-check customs declaration data with physical freight manifests, exit records, and recipient-country entry evidence. If the exporter cannot substantiate the physical departure of the goods or the non-EU establishment of the service recipient, the zero-rating is retroactively disallowed, and the exporter must pay the missing 20% French VAT and file an amended VAT return. Where the French tax authority finds a deliberate misstatement, the statutory penalties under Articles 1728 to 1729 CGI include: late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.20% per month; a 5% to 10% penalty for late filing, increasing to 40% for insufficient declarations; a 40% penalty for deliberate inaccuracies; and an 80% penalty for abusive scheme or organized fraud. Criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI may lead to a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years. False customs declarations are also sanctionable under the Customs Code Articles 414 to 416 with confiscation of the goods and fines of up to twice the value of the fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the national central bank, the exclusive issuer of euro banknotes, the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistical compilation, and the supervisory coordinator for payment systems. Licensing and prudential/AML enforcement for credit institutions is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution). Residual exchange-control policy powers rest with the Direction Générale du Trésor under the Code monétaire et financier, particularly Articles L151-1 to L165-1.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a founding member of the Eurozone; the euro is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account in accordance with TFEU Articles 63-66 on the free movement of capital. There is no prior exchange-control approval requirement for inbound FDI into an SARL, for profit remittances to non-resident shareholders, or for payment of cross-border trade invoices. Legal restrictions are limited to EU autonomous sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, and balance-of-payments statistical reporting. Profit remittance is unrestricted; however, dividends paid by an SARL to non-resident shareholders may be subject to withholding tax under Article 119 quater CGI unless reduced by an applicable double taxation treaty. Enterprises must maintain documentary evidence of the underlying transaction and comply with ACPR customer due diligence when any transfer reaches mandatory reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France abolished its exchange-control surrender regime under Ordonnance n° 67-1121 of 22 December 1967 and fully liberalized external transactions under Loi n° 86-793 of 25 July 1986. There is no statutory deadline requiring repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio of foreign currency receipts into euros. An exporting SARL may lawfully retain USD or other foreign currency balances in authorized foreign-currency compte devises at a licensed French credit institution and may convert them at its own commercial discretion. The sole ongoing obligation is indirect statistical reporting: French banks transmit cross-border payment data to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes when monthly transaction volumes exceed thresholds set by the Bank; this is a reporting requirement, not a surrender or conversion rule.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_reporting_obligation: Under Article L152-1 of the Code monétaire et financier, all transfers of funds between France and foreign countries of an amount equal to or exceeding de-minimis regulatory thresholds must be declared to the Banque de France through the financial intermediary. For a creative-services SARL receiving USD settlement from overseas game publishers, the bank will file the BDR declaration automatically; the SARL should retain the invoice, contract, and proof-of-service in its treasury files to reconcile with the bank's reference code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.merchant_of_record_and_paypal_fx_framewo: Where PayPal is used as a secondary settlement rail, PayPal operates under a French e-money licence (via PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie, S.C.A., passported in France) and performs the currency conversion at its own published exchange rate plus margin. Under French consumer and commercial codes, the SARL must treat PayPal balances as safeguarded e-money, not bank deposits, and must keep separate internal records of FX conversion costs and losses for transfer-pricing and treasury-optimization purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Professional Operating Account (Compte Courant Professionnel) and dedicated Capital Escrow Sub-Account for share capital blockage
Business Current Account (Compte Professionnel) plus Capital Locked Account (Compte de Dépôt du Capital) for constitution
Operating Current Account for the SARL and segregated Escrow Cell for capital injection verification
Corporate Current Account and Investment/Giro sub-ledger for treasury sweeps
Corporate Current Account (Compte de Dépôt du Professionnel) with limited foreign-currency capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for licensed French payment institutions and e-money institutions such as Qonto and Shine, which offer full French IBANs, robust API treasury feeds, and smooth AML onboarding for low-risk creative BPO entities. Medium for passported EU EMIs such as Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bunq, which retain fiduciary safeguarding accounts at partner banks and may restrict certain payment purposes. Low for offshore digital EMIs and UK-centred neo-banks after Brexit, as they generally cannot hold dedicated French IBANs nor access the Banque de France retail payment system directly; any reliance on such entities must be structured via a French licensed intermediary. Legal constraint: EMIs cannot grant credit and, under the e-money directive transposed into Articles L525-4 and following of the Code monétaire et financier, client funds must be safeguarded in a segregated account, which may complicate high-value escrow and capital-blocage procedures. Recommended architecture: a licensed Tier-1 French commercial bank as the primary clearing account, with one domestic EMI wallet for operational convenience and PayPal as an invoice-level settlement gateway for small contracts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law permits both physical and remote onboarding. Under ACPR guidance dated 7 July 2020, video-identification and digital KYC are legally valid for opening a SARL account, provided identity verification is performed via a regulated electronic identification solution with live video, document capture, and liveness checks. Nevertheless, in practice the majority of Tier-1 banks require at least one physical visit by the gérant (statutory manager) to sign the account agreement, especially when the SARL is newly formed, has non-resident shareholders, or lacks an established credit file. For a fully non-resident management team, French banks accept onboarding through a notarized power of attorney in favour of a local representative, with apostillization and sworn French translation of the corporate documents. The safest mandate: the gérant attends a physical interview at the chosen branch, or engages in a certified remote video interview via a compliant third-party identity provider, and all partners/UBOs submit certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and source-of-funds evidence before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership: SARL shares held by non-resident individuals or by an intermediate entity in a non-EU jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing extract from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; completed UBO identification form listing every natural person holding or controlling more than 25% of shares or voting rights; certified passports and proof-of-address for all UBOs; ownership chain chart from ultimate shareholder to SARL; apostilled and sworn-translated corporate certificates for any foreign intermediate entity; if the intermediate entity is in a high-risk jurisdiction, an additional professional attestation from a licensed fiduciary or financial intermediary verifying the economic substance of that entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable digital commercial activity: a 3D art and rigging studio without physical storefront, with most counterparties being overseas game developers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office proof in the form of a commercial lease (bail commercial) or an approved domiciliation contract under Article L123-11-2 of the Code de commerce; URSSAF registration confirmation and SIREN/SIRET/Kbis extracts; signed Master Service Agreements (MSA) and purchase orders with at least two AAA game studios; project portfolio with client delivery evidence (ArtStation, Steam product acknowledgment, work-commission emails); corporate website and LinkedIn profile; 12-month cash-flow forecast and business plan; pro-forma and issued invoices showing the commercial model of 'Creative_Game_Art_BPO'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the opening capital injection and for large inbound wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed and dated origin-of-funds declaration (source des fonds); 12-month bank statements from each contributing shareholder; deed of transfer or share subscription (acte de souscription) referencing the exact amount wired; if capital contribution is in kind, a statutory auditor's valuation report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) or a sworn valuation document; tax identification and residency proof for each contributor conditioned on the treaty network; written explanation of the economic purpose of the capital injection and its correlation with the business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP screening, and adverse-media hits on shareholders or ultimate counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean result letters from EU consolidated financial-sanctions screening and OFAC screening; PEP self-declaration signed by every UBO; board statement confirming the entity is not owned or controlled by a sanctioned person; certified identities with voluminous biometric and address evidence; explanation letter if a partial name-match arises, supported by Article L561-6 due-diligence record; evidence of the lawful source of wealth for any flagged shareholder, including tax filings, dividend vouchers, or asset-transfer deeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perception of the SARL as a zero-employee shell created solely to route funds from foreign publishers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis showing ISIC 7490 classification and registered activity in game-asset production; subcontracting or employment contracts with the actual 3D modellers and riggers; ergonomic evidence of service delivery such as signed work acceptances and version-control server logs; tax, social-security, and VAT registrations confirming operating substance; updated statutes showing clear profit-objective and budget; if required, a written letter from the external chartered accountant validating the economic reality of the structure and its pricing under arm's-length principles.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for a non-resident shareholder wiring capital to FR_SARL: (1) execute the SARL statutes and, if applicable, use the bank's dedicated capital escrow account opened in the company's name; (2) transmit a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank with a clear purpose reference to the corporate deed, using the Banque de France balance-of-payments classification code for capital operations (category 'Investment — capital of companies', code 301 under the BDR framework); (3) ensure the instruction identifies the SARL by exact legal name, SIREN number, and French IBAN beginning with FR76; (4) the receiving bank will require, as verification, the Kbis extract, the executed statutes, the RBE filing, the identity of the transferring shareholder, and the source-of-funds evidence; (5) for amounts exceeding prevailing ACPR/statistical thresholds, the bank files a balance-of-payments declaration and may request a formal declaration of fund origin under Article L561-15 of the Code monétaire et financier; (6) upon receipt, the account is credited to the capital sub-ledger and may be used only after verification of the legal capital obligation, with any surplus held in a current-account shareholder loan recorded by a written convention de compte courant; (7) for all future invoices, inbound USD payments from overseas publishers are routed via SWIFT MT103 with settlement through the correspondent banking network and converted to EUR at the bank's commercial rate or via a pre-agreed FX forward.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail hierarchy for the SARL's outflows: primary rail is the SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA SCT and SEPA Instant) for EUR disbursements to European contractors and domestic suppliers, providing same-day or immediate settlement with full IBAN validation; international non-EUR disbursements use SWIFT MT103 with MT202 COV cover payments, ensuring correspondent-bank transparency and fee predictability; for high-value contract settlements to overseas game-art subcontractors, the SARL may establish an irrevocable confirmed documentary letter of credit (Commercial LC) at its Tier-1 bank, with presentation of invoices, artwork-delivery acceptance certificates, and the applicable INCOTERMS 2020 clause (e.g., DAP or EXW); PayPal Business serves as a fallback micro-rail for engagements below EUR 2,500 or for clients mandating PayPal settlement, subject to PayPal's KYC on each counterparty and its own FX conversion margin; all outbound wires must reference the underlying commercial invoice and be matched in the treasury file with the purchase order and proof-of-delivery. It is legally impermissible to mix personal funds with corporate treasury; inter-company payments to related entities must be supported by a formal services agreement and arm's-length invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright FX forward (change à terme ferme) executed with a licensed French credit institution, covering confirmed USD receivables from overseas game publishers without requiring any regulatory authorization.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) denominated in restricted or exotic currencies (for example BRL, KRW, INR or onshore CNY) where physical delivery is legally impossible; permitted when the reference currency exposure arises from a bona fide commercial service contract.

European-style plain vanilla FX options (change optionnel à prime octroyée) purchased to cap adverse USD/EUR moves while retaining upside, treated as an eligible hedge of the SARL's trade-debt portfolio.
Cross-currency swap (XCCY) concluded under an ISDA-style master agreement converting a USD-denominated receivable or liability stream into EUR cash flows for multi-year studio agreements.

FX swap (change de devises simultané) used for short-term liquidity management, converting temporary EUR excess balances into USD only when a corresponding USD payment is due within the swap's ten-month window.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.treasury_sweep_and_currency_concentratio: All foreign-currency receipts are swept weekly into the primary EUR operating account to minimize idle foreign balances in bank and PayPal wallets. The SARL must maintain a written treasury policy stating the maximum un-hedged USD exposure (typically not to exceed EUR 50,000 of open exposure) and defining the monthly hedging process: invoices over EUR 20,000 are hedged via an outright forward matching the expected settlement date, while smaller invoices are netted into a monthly rolling forward. Monthly reconciliation of PayPal, EMI, and bank balances is mandatory to ensure no mixed funding and to substantiate arm's-length FX pricing for French transfer-pricing audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.escrow_and_capital_blockage_procedure: For the statutory capital release at constitution, funds must be blocked until the entity files its RCS registration and the bank receives the attestation of capital deposit from the notary or the legal-rep certificate. After confirmation, the capital is released into the operational current account, and the bank issues the certificat de dépôt des fonds required for the Greffe application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (French corporate income tax return, Form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, e-filing due by the second business day after 1 May (typically 2-15 May)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% surcharge (40% if formal demand fails); 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; possible administrative assessment if omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory deposit of annual financial statements after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) via Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit to the Greffe within 1 month of approval (maximum 7 months)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 4,500 against the gérant; judicial injunction to file; persistent non-compliance can lead to RCS administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution declaration (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, Form 1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 December for the following tax year's assessment basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% surcharge; 40% after formal notice; 0.20% monthly interest; enforced collection measures if unpaid.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SARL when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets above EUR 4.5 million, net turnover above EUR 9 million, average permanent staff above 50. Also triggered if shareholders holding at least 1/10th of capital petition or under group consolidation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG) for individual annual financial statements; IFRS permitted only for consolidated accounts if elected under applicable rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The gérant must confirm the accuracy of the beneficial-owner register at each annual shareholders' meeting. Any subsequent change in beneficial ownership or shareholding triggering a UBO update must be filed with the Greffe du RCS within 30 days. There is no standalone annual UBO filing; correctness is verified during the annual corporate maintenance and RCS update process.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of directors and legal representatives
Minute book (Registre de procès-verbaux des assemblées et assemblée générale)
Register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Share-transfer and pledge register (Registre des mouvements de titres et nantissements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 750 per annum for a commercial registered-office address and professional corporate-agent correspondence handling in common business districts
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required below statutory thresholds; when mandatory, roughly USD 5,500 - 16,500 per audit depending on company size and external auditor rates

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) up to 30% of qualifying expenses; no general tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Formulaire 1200) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for FY ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities, report attributable French source income only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for French tax adjustments and TP adjustments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay, minimum €150, maximum 10% of tax due; plus interest on late payments

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from French tax authorities and submit with TRC application to reduce WHT rate under applicable DTA; file via impots.gouv.fr portal
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs; Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0% under most DTAs

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million annual consolidated group turnover for mandatory Local File and Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France adheres to OECD BEPS Action 5; Economic Substance Regulations require adequate substance for tax residency in certain cases, particularly for holding or IP entities, but standard operational substance required for French tax residency

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 500% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution of evaded amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, civil restitution orders, and potential disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or provide TP documentation or using non-arm's length pricing without justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 100% of the tax adjustment, plus interest; possible criminal sanctions in aggravated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors who approved non-compliant arrangements; potential fines and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Taxes on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-remittance of WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident recipients
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 10% to 40% of the unpaid WHT, plus interest and possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid taxes; potential jail time and travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company or Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SARL without genuine business operations or substance to justify tax residency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dissolution of the company, back taxes, penalties up to 10% of turnover, and potential criminal liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil leading to personal liability for debts and taxes; possible imprisonment for fraudulent management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with French AML/CTF obligations or sanctions screening in cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover, plus potential criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment, and disqualification from corporate roles
